item.title: [New] Microsoft Threat Intelligence analyses a malicious Claude Code-branded editor extension that plants a persistent SSH backdoor
item.description:
Developer workstations hold cloud tokens and signing keys; an AI-assistant lookalike extension with SSH persistence gives an attacker a durable foothold that endpoint baselines rarely watch.

Threat Intel · Read the post's detection and remediation guidance, inventory editor extensions on developer devices, and hunt for unexpected SSH authorized_keys changes or new SSH listeners on them.

item.title: [Due in 1 day] Defender for Servers stops billing Windows 10/11 and other desktops as servers on 1 November and counts every machine separately, golden-image clones included
item.description:
Multi-session and VDI hosts protected today through Defender for Servers Plan 1 move to a Defender for Endpoint licensing route; a host that falls between the two is where coverage silently lapses.

Azure · deadline 2026-11-01 · Before 1 November list Plan 1 machines whose OS is a client SKU (including AVD multi-session) and confirm each has a Defender for Endpoint licence; check golden-image clones that share an Arc ID, because each now counts separately.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [New] Defender XDR advanced hunting gets a CallActivityEvents table for suspicious Teams calls and meetings, GA early to mid November 2026
item.description:
Teams-call vishing and help-desk impersonation from external tenants had no hunting table of its own; this one gives the initiator's tenant and membership type, the fields an external-impersonation detection needs.

Defender XDR · Review the CallActivityEvents schema on Learn, plan a detection for external-tenant initiators joined to MessageEvents on ThreadId, and check that the Sentinel or streaming-API ingestion picks the table up once it appears.

Open in the Microsoft SOC Brief · Microsoft source

item.title: [Due in 1 day] Security Operator loses default access to email threat policies and the Tenant Allow/Block List under Defender Unified RBAC, from early November
item.description:
Adding a block entry to the Tenant Allow/Block List is a routine containment step in a phishing incident. An analyst who holds only Security Operator will find that step denied mid-incident some day in November, with no error that names this change.

Defender XDR · deadline 2026-11-01 · List who holds Entra Security Operator and uses it for email threat policies or the Tenant Allow/Block List; before November assign those people the Unified RBAC permissions Core security settings and Detection tuning, or a role that includes them, and test a block entry with a Security Operator-only account.

item.title: [New] Defender for Identity's 'operating system that will soon become unsupported' health alert now names Windows Server 2016; sensors keep reporting after its extended support ends
item.description:
Domain controllers still on Windows Server 2016 will start raising this health alert, and after 12 January 2027 parts of the sensor's detection may silently degrade on them while the sensor still shows as healthy and reporting.

MDI · List sensors by OS version in the Defender portal (Settings > Identities > Sensors), plan the upgrade of every Windows Server 2016 domain controller, AD FS and AD CS host before 12 January 2027, and treat the new health alert as a tracked work item rather than noise.

item.title: [New] Sentinel Azure Storage Blob connector troubleshooting now names the storage roles the connector's service principal needs, and adds an Event Grid cause
item.description:
A blob connector that stops ingesting is a silent log-source gap; Microsoft now states the exact roles the service principal needs, so a missing assignment is checkable.

Sentinel · On every storage account a Sentinel blob connector reads, confirm the connector's service principal holds Storage Blob Data Reader and Storage Queue Data Contributor, and that the Event Grid subscription shows delivered events.

item.description:

item.title: [New] Defender's new Threat intelligence experience: Overview and Intel explorer replace the Threat analytics and Intel management pages; Threat analytics types are renamed (Actor to Threat actor, Activity to Campaign, Technique to Attack patterns)
item.description:
Runbooks, bookmarks and analyst training that point at Threat analytics or Intel management stop matching the portal, and reports filed under Actor, Activity or Technique are now found under Threat actor, Campaign and Attack patterns.

Defender XDR · Update the TI runbook and analyst bookmarks to Threat intelligence > Overview and Intel explorer, and re-check any email notification and custom-detection links that pointed at Threat analytics reports.

item.title: [New] Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 adds a Move to Quarantine remediation action: admins can pull suspicious mail from mailboxes into Defender quarantine, rollout early November to mid-December 2026
item.description:
It is a reversible containment option between Move to Junk and Soft/Hard delete: the evidence stays reviewable and releasable, and the action is audited in the Action Center, so phishing response no longer has to choose between leaving mail in reach of the user and destroying it.

Defender XDR · Before November decide which quarantine policy the action should use, confirm who holds Search and Purge, and add Move to Quarantine to the phishing and BEC playbooks as the default containment step.

item.title: [Message Center] MC1523084 Microsoft Defender for Office 365: Move email messages to quarantine with a new remediation action
item.description:
Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Plan 2 introduces a new "Move to Quarantine" remediation action allowing admins to move suspicious emails from user mailboxes to Defender quarantine for safer investigation and management. It rolls out worldwide from November to December 2026, requiring no user action but recommended policy reviews and training updates.
